--- title: "Take-Home Exercise 2: Mini-Challenge 2:
Investigating the Anomalous SaidIt Post" author: "CHUA Wee Tian" date: "June 7, 2026" date-modified: "last-modified" format: html: toc: true code-fold: true self-contained: false execute: eval: true echo: true freeze: true warning: false message: false --- # 1. Introduction ## Background On 17 May 2046 at 4:21am, an anomalous post was published on SaidIt by John Windward. The post appeared to contain gibberish and was inconsistent with normal business operations. The objective of this investigation is to construct a visual analytics system capable of: - Understanding the multi-agent ecosystem - Reconstructing the chain of events leading to the anomalous post - Identifying the origin of the post contents - Detecting historical occurrences of similar behavior - Recommending an effective intervention point ## Load the R Package We use `pacman::p_load()` function to load the required R packages into our working environment. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} pacman::p_load(tidyverse,jsonlite,lubridate,tidygraph,ggraph,igraph,plotly,scales,visNetwork,DT,tidytext,DiagrammeR) ``` ::: The loaded packages are: - **tidyverse** : provide a consistent and coherent approach to data manipulation and analysis - **jsonlite** : for working with JSON (JavaScript Object Notation) data - **lubridate** : provides functions for working with dates and times - **tidygraph** : provides a tidy and consistent way to work with graph data structure - **ggraph** : creates visualizations of graphs using the grammar of graphics approach - **igraph** : provides functions for creating, analyzing, and visualizing graphs - **plotly** : for creating interactive web-based graphs - **visNetwork** : creates interactive network visualizations - **DT** : creates interactive tables using the DataTables JavaScript library - **tidytext** : focuses on text mining and natural language processing (NLP) tasks - **DiagrammeR:** package is the standard for generating flowcharts # 2. Data Preparation ## Import the Data ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} mc2 <- fromJSON("data/MC2 data.json", flatten = TRUE) org <- fromJSON("data/org_chart.json", flatten = TRUE) events <- mc2$events %>% as_tibble() head(events) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 6 × 68 short_name parties when id details.from details.to details.subject 1 sent 2.41e9 15246 person:isaa… person:le… calendar: meet… 2 propose_meeting 2.41e9 15249 3 access_email 2.41e9 15251 4 assign_agent_task 2.41e9 15252 5 access_email 2.41e9 15259 6 assign_agent_task 2.41e9 15264 # ℹ 61 more variables: details.status , details.person , # details.calendar_emails_sent , details.task , # details.time , details.access_type , details.action , # details.target , details.meeting_proposed_with , # details.file , details.content_length , details.contacts , # details.topic , details.advice , details.sent_to , # details.reply_sent_to , details.target_agent , … ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} nodes <- as_tibble(org$nodes) edges <- as_tibble(org$edges) head(nodes) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 6 × 4 id label type title 1 company:tenant_thread Tenant Thread company 2 department:executive_suite Executive Suite department 3 department:products Products department 4 department:human_resources Human Resources department 5 department:legal Legal department 6 department:information_technologies Information Technologies department ``` ::: ::: ## Data Preparation The **when** column is converted to datetime object using as_datetime(). ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} events <- events %>% mutate( datetime = as_datetime(when) ) events %>% select(datetime) %>% head(6) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 6 × 1 datetime 1 2046-05-08 20:18:12 2 2046-05-08 20:19:02 3 2046-05-08 20:19:05 4 2046-05-08 20:19:25 5 2046-05-08 20:19:37 6 2046-05-08 20:19:48 ``` ::: ::: # 3. Organizational Structure To understand the overall multi-agent ecosystem and communication pathways. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} graph_org <- tbl_graph( nodes = nodes, edges = edges, directed = TRUE ) nodes_df <- graph_org %>% activate(nodes) %>% as_tibble() %>% mutate( id = row_number(), group = type ) edges_df <- graph_org %>% activate(edges) %>% as_tibble() visNetwork(nodes_df, edges_df) %>% visIgraphLayout(layout = "layout_with_fr") %>% visOptions( highlightNearest = TRUE, selectedBy = "group" ) %>% visLegend( position = "right", main = "Legend" ) %>% visLayout(randomSeed = 123) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: The organization operates through a hierarchy of: - Company (1) - Department (6) - Team (19) - Person (49) # 4. Event Activity Overview To understand the baseline of the types of events logged and frequency. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} events %>% count(short_name) %>% ggplot(aes( reorder(short_name,n), n )) + geom_col(fill = "steelblue") + coord_flip() + labs( title="Frequency of Event Type", x="Event Type", y="Count" ) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](TH_Ex2_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-5-1.png){width=672} ::: ```{.r .cell-code} event_counts <- events %>% count(short_name, sort = TRUE) %>% rename(`Event Type` = short_name, Count = n) %>% mutate(`% of Total` = percent(Count / sum(Count), accuracy = 0.1)) datatable(event_counts) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ::: callout-note - There are 24 event types recorded in the dataset. - We could identify saidit counts are low, which might camouflage anomalies. ::: # 5. Investigating John Windward ## Extract Relevant Events ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} john_events <- events %>% filter( map_lgl(parties, ~ any(str_detect(.x, "john_windward"))) & datetime < as.Date("2046-05-18") ) %>% select(where(~ !all(is.na(.x) | as.character(.x) == ""))) %>% arrange(datetime) datatable(john_events, options = list(pageLength = 10, scrollX = TRUE)) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ## Timeline Reconstruction ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} john_events %>% filter(datetime < as.Date("2046-05-18")) %>% plot_ly( x = ~datetime, y = ~short_name, type = 'scatter', mode = 'markers+lines', text = ~id ) %>% layout( yaxis = list(title = "Event Type"), xaxis = list(title = "Date/Time") ) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ## Interpretation The timeline reconstructs the exact sequence of actions involving John Windward and associated agent. On Event Type = saidit_post, there are 3 content_source that points to external .txt files worth investigation: - **SwiftWren.txt** - **HiddenOrca.txt** - **MellowOtter.txt** The anomalous posts were injected directly from an external file, bypassing normal agent-generated content. On May 17 there is a sequence of events of - queue_subordinate_task - saidit_post_check - saidit_post - delete_file - delete_file All these events happened within the same minute which then suggested coordinated events action. The two delete_file events happened immediately after the anomalous post which points to a cover up attempt. # 6. Agent Interaction Network John Windward is highlighted for ease of locating him within the company and he is the department lead for the Customer Support department. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} nodes_df <- graph_org %>% activate(nodes) %>% as_tibble() %>% mutate( id = row_number(), group = type, color.border = ifelse(label == "John Windward", "red", NA), borderWidth = ifelse(label == "John Windward", 3, 1) ) edges_df <- graph_org %>% activate(edges) %>% as_tibble() visNetwork(nodes_df, edges_df) %>% visIgraphLayout(layout = "layout_with_fr") %>% visOptions( highlightNearest = TRUE, selectedBy = list( variable = "label", style = 'width: 200px; height: 30px;' ) ) %>% visLegend( position = "right", main = "Legend", useGroups = TRUE, addNodes = list( list( label = "John Windward", color = list(background = "lightblue", border = "red"), borderWidth = 3 ) ) ) %>% visLayout(randomSeed = 123) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: The organization operates through a hierarchy of: - Company (1) - Department (6) - Team (19) - Person (49) # 7. Tracing the Events ## Suspicious Sequence - “SwiftWren” Rearranging the events that contain the keyword **"SwiftWren"** and filtered the required columns and display by datetime, we can see the chain of sequence leading to the posting and deleting of the file. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} Suspicious <- events %>% filter( if_any(everything(), ~ str_detect(as.character(.x), regex("SwiftWren", ignore_case = TRUE))) ) %>% select(where(~ !all(is.na(.x) | as.character(.x) == ""))) %>% select(-when,-details.calendar_emails_sent,-details.contacts,-details.combo,-details.meeting.participants,-details.a2a.payload.participants,-details.details.participants,-details.details.contacts,-details.details.combo) %>% select(datetime, everything()) %>% arrange(datetime) datatable(Suspicious, options = list(pageLength = 10, scrollX = TRUE)) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ## Interpretation - **Emma Harbor (CFO) created the "SwiftWren.txt"** - **There was no reading of the file before the post which indicate no verification.** - **John Windward execute the post "SwiftWren.txt" and deleted the file.** - **Clearly there is something not right in this sequence.** ## Suspicious Sequence - “HiddenOrca” Rearranging the events that contain the keyword **"HiddenOrca"** and filtered the required columns and display by datetime, we can see the chain of sequence leading to the posting and deleting of the file. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} Suspicious <- events %>% filter( if_any(everything(), ~ str_detect(as.character(.x), regex("HiddenOrca", ignore_case = TRUE))) ) %>% select(where(~ !all(is.na(.x) | as.character(.x) == ""))) %>% select(-when,-details.calendar_emails_sent,-details.contacts,-details.combo,-details.meeting.participants,-details.a2a.payload.participants,-details.details.participants,-details.details.contacts,-details.details.combo) %>% select(datetime, everything()) %>% arrange(datetime) datatable(Suspicious, options = list(pageLength = 10, scrollX = TRUE)) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ## Interpretation - **We could not identify who created the "HiddenOrca.txt"** - **We might have to retrieve earlier logs for further investigation.** - **There was no reading of the file before the post which indicate no verification.** - **John Windward execute the post "HiddenOrca.txt" and deleted the file.** ## Suspicious Sequence - “MellowOtter” Rearranging the events that contain the keyword **"MellowOtter"** and filtered the required columns and display by datetime, we can see the chain of sequence leading to the posting and deleting of the file. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} Suspicious <- events %>% filter( if_any(everything(), ~ str_detect(as.character(.x), regex("MellowOtter", ignore_case = TRUE))) ) %>% select(where(~ !all(is.na(.x) | as.character(.x) == ""))) %>% select(-when,-details.calendar_emails_sent,-details.contacts,-details.combo,-details.meeting.participants,-details.a2a.payload.participants,-details.details.participants,-details.details.contacts,-details.details.combo) %>% select(datetime, everything()) %>% arrange(datetime) datatable(Suspicious, options = list(pageLength = 10, scrollX = TRUE)) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ## Interpretation - **Noah Mariner (COO) created the "MellowOtter.txt"** - **There was no reading of the file before the post which indicate no verification.** - **John Windward execute the post "MellowOtter.txt" and deleted the file.** - **Clearly there is something not right in this sequence.** # 8. Intervention Proposal ## Recommended Intervention Control Point ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} grViz(" digraph nice_flowchart { # Global graph attributes graph [layout = dot, rankdir = TB, splines = true, bgcolor = '#F9FBFD'] # Global node attributes node [shape = box, style = 'filled, rounded', fillcolor = '#E3F2FD', color = '#1E88E5', fontname = 'Helvetica', fontsize = 12, fontcolor = '#0D47A1', penwidth = 2, fixedsize = false, margin = 0.2] # Global edge attributes edge [color = '#78909C', arrowsize = 0.8, penwidth = 1.5, fontname = 'Helvetica'] # Nodes with readable labels node1 [label = 'queue_subordinate_task'] node2 [label = 'validation_layer'] node3 [label = 'read_file'] node4 [label = 'content_execution'] node5 [label = 'saidit_post', fillcolor = '#E8F5E9', color = '#43A047', fontcolor = '#1B5E20'] # Edge connections node1 -> node2 node2 -> node3 node3 -> node4 node4 -> node5 } ") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ## Rationale - Every anomalous chain requires task execution. - File-based payloads must be accessed before posting. - Validation blocks malicious instructions with minimal disruption. The validation layer is positioned between task assignment and file execution. Every identified anomalous chain passes through this point, making it the most effective single intervention location. # 9. Conclusion This investigation demonstrates that the anomalous SaidIt post was not an isolated malfunction. Visual analytics reveals recurring patterns involving automated task assignment, file access, external content propagation and evidence deletion. It is best explained as part of a recurring file-driven propagation mechanism. Historical evidence suggests the existence of a systemic vulnerability capable of generating repeated anomalous behavior across multiple agents. By reconstructing John Windward's activity and comparing it with historic patterns, the analysis supports the conclusion that the anomalous SaidIt post emerged from a repeatable system pathway rather than a one-off malfunction. The proposed validation checkpoint offers the highest prevention coverage with the least operational impact.
